newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian avge lending rate down to 9.7 vs 11.2 pct.
newsitem.headline: Croatian avge lending rate down to 9.7 vs 11.2 pct.

text.p: The Croatian average lending rate slipped to 9.7 percent on Tuesday from 11.2 percent the previous day amid slightly improved liquidity.
The day's total settlements were put at 57.5 million kuna against 61.5 million kuna demand.
Fresh loans accounted for 44.8 million kuna trade and were mostly call money loans granted at an unchanged 10.5 percent, with a single loan being struck at 11 percent and granted to a savings bank.
Short-term funds were granted at 11 percent for 10-day borrowings and 13 percent for one-month.
Insurers extended previous one-week and nine-day loans at a steady 9.0 percent.
The central bank calculated its kuna midrates for Wednesday weaker at 6.0761 against the dollar and firmer at 3.5771 against the German mark. -- Sandra Kalogjera, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
